Triggers.value: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Threat.value: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened

vignette: Rohan had always taken pride in his small shop, where he spent most of his days surrounded by the familiar smells of spices and fresh produce. But since the night his partner, Amir, had attacked him, everything felt different. The scent of sweat or body odor would suddenly transport Rohan back to that moment, making his heart racing and palms sweating. It was as if his body was constantly on high alert, waiting for the next threat. One day, while restocking shelves, a stranger approached him, asking for directions. Rohan's instincts kicked in, and he felt an intense sense of danger, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. He couldn't shake off the feeling that this person might be a threat, just like Amir had been. As he tried to compose himself, he caught a whiff of the stranger's sweat and was instantly flooded with memories of that fateful night. The memories came without warning, triggered by the smallest details. A conversation about relationships or trust would send him spiraling back to the moments leading up to the attack. Rohan would feel a wave of rage wash over him, making it hard to breathe. He couldn't understand why his body kept reacting as if he was still in danger, even when he knew he was safe. Rohan struggled with feelings of guilt and self-doubt. He couldn't forgive himself for not fighting back or escaping sooner. "If only I had been stronger," he would tell himself, "this wouldn't have happened." These thoughts swirled in his mind like a toxic cycle, making him question his own ability to protect himself. As the days turned into weeks, Rohan found it increasingly difficult to sleep. He would lie awake at night, his senses on high alert, waiting for any sign of danger. His relationship with his new partner began to suffer as he became withdrawn and irritable. The memories of that night lingered, haunting him like a ghost. Rohan's body seemed to have developed a mind of its own. He would experience intense emotional episodes without any clear memory or trigger. It was as if his emotions had become disconnected from his rational thinking. This made him feel even more powerless and trapped in his own skin. As the cycle continued, Rohan began to notice that certain conversation topics would leave him feeling raw and exposed. Discussing relationships or trust with friends and family became increasingly difficult. The memories of Amir's words, the way he had manipulated and controlled Rohan, came flooding back. It was as if the wounds were still open, refusing to heal. One evening, while closing up his shop, Rohan realized that he couldn't keep living like this. He knew he needed help to break free from the cycle of fear and guilt. As he locked the door, he felt a glimmer of hope - maybe, just maybe, he could learn to trust himself again and find a way to heal. Rohan's partner encouraged him to seek therapy, but he was afraid of confronting his demons head-on. What if he couldn't handle the emotions that came flooding back? What if he wasn't strong enough to face his fears? Despite these doubts, Rohan knew he had to try - for himself, and for those who cared about him.
